source.version: ACM published version of record, CI '25: Proceedings of the ACM Collective Intelligence Conference, printed pp. 297–316, DOI 10.1145/3715928.3737486. ACM cover states Published: 04 August 2025 and PDF Download: 16 December 2025. The cover is PDF p. 1.
source.supplement_used: Appendix A.1–A.6 in the same PDF, PDF pp. 15–21 (printed pp. 310–316), including task instructions, prompts, homogenization analysis and figures, and surveys. No separate supplement or posted raw data used.

studies.label: Dyadic brainstorming: conversational cues by meeting modality
studies.cluster_se_treatment: The assigned condition is shared by both members of a dyad. The idea-topic, conversation-topic, and idea-count REML analyses use group outcomes, with Access-to-Cue, Modality and their interaction as fixed effects and Prior Design Experience and Recycling Knowledge as random effects. The numerical topic tests are interpreted as analyses with one observation per dyad; no separately clustered SE is printed. The idea-homogenization analysis instead compares individual idea distances with a Wilcoxon test; no test result or dyad adjustment is reported. Sources: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 298), Sec. 1; PDF p. 7 (printed p. 302), Sec. 5.1.1; PDF p. 9 (printed p. 304), Secs. 5.1.2-5.1.3; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 306), Sec. 6.3.

counts_source.quote: We recruited 172 participants, randomly assigned to four conditions; Cue-Virtual, Cue-InPerson, NoCue-Virtual, and NoCue-InPerson to participate in a brainstorming discussion with one other participant (in 86 dyads).

arms.name: Cue-Virtual
arms.description: Dyad partners in separate rooms used CueTip video conferencing and shared notes; GPT-4o-mini generated a short contextual cue every minute, displayed with a visual notification and audio chime.

arms.name: Cue-InPerson
arms.description: Dyad partners in the same room used CueTip and shared notes; the video call window was inactive. The cue content and delivery mechanism matched Cue-Virtual.

arms.name: NoCue-Virtual
arms.description: Dyad partners in separate rooms used the same video conferencing and shared-note interface without conversational cues.

arms.name: NoCue-InPerson
arms.description: Dyad partners in the same room used the same shared-note interface without conversational cues.

studies.task: Dyads brainstormed alternative uses for recyclable trash from a beach cleanup, recording ideas as bullet points in shared notes during a 20-minute task with 15 minutes for generation and 5 for selecting the best idea (PDF p. 15, printed p. 310, App. A.2.2).

ai_tool.name: CueTip using OpenAI GPT-4o-mini
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 300), Secs. 3.2.2, 3.3 and 4.1.2; the model release year is not stated in the paper.

estimates.outcome: Topic diversity of generated ideas (Shannon entropy)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Ideas were pooled across groups to fit BERTopic with HDBSCAN; Shannon entropy from scipy was used for topic diversity. The result compares dyad-level idea collections. The paper does not clearly explain aggregation from ideas to the dyad score: Sec. 4.1.4 says each idea's topic diversity score, whereas Sec. 5.1.1 and Fig. 5a compare groups.

sources.quote: [F(1, 67.03) = 6.51, p = 0.013] between the groups with cues (μ = 2.3, SD = 0.3) and without cues (μ = 2.1, SD = 0.4)

sources.locator: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 302), Sec. 5.1.1; corroborated by PDF p. 8 (printed p. 303), Fig. 5a
sources.quote: A Tukey’s HSD post hoc test on the ‘Access-to-Cue’ factor confirmed a statistically significant difference (p ≈ 0.012), as shown in fig.5a.

estimates.notes: The F test is the full-sample Access-to-Cue main effect, pooling meeting modalities. REML fixed effects are Access-to-Cue, Modality and their interaction; random effects are prior design experience and recycling knowledge. No coefficient, SE, CI, standardized effect or analyzed arm count is printed. The reported SDs concern dyad scores; sd_level is null because the specified vocabulary has no team category. Flexibility denotes topical variety within each dyad's idea collection; this is not the across-dyad homogenization outcome. The paper calls the dependent variable 'topic diversity of cues', an apparent wording error because the comparison includes NoCue groups. The Tukey HSD p value is preserved in the additional source quotation for this same contrast; it is not a separate estimate. The figure caption prints its post hoc p value as an equality, whereas the text marks it approximate. The labeled box-plot summaries are not arm means or SDs, and no values are estimated from the plot.

estimates.outcome: Topic diversity of the conversation transcript (unique IAB top-level topics)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Assembly AI transcribed ideation audio and mapped utterances to the IAB topic taxonomy. The paper counted unique top-level topics for each speaker and conversational round, then used their combined set across rounds as the conversation's final topic-diversity score. One conversation score represents the dyad.

This is coded other because the scored output is the entire spoken discussion, rather than only the submitted ideas, and it is retained as in the reconciled screening form. The F test is the full-sample Access-to-Cue main effect, pooling modalities. REML fixed effects are Access-to-Cue, Modality and their interaction; random effects are prior design experience and recycling knowledge. The reported SDs concern dyad conversation scores; sd_level is null because the specified vocabulary has no team category. No SE, CI, coefficient, standardized effect or analyzed count is printed. estimates.outcome: Number of ideas generated per dyad
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: A researcher removed duplicate ideas from each session's notes, consulted another researcher on ambiguous cases, and supplemented missing ideas from recordings and transcripts. The score was the count of bullet points in the classified notes.

sources.quote: Groups with cues did not generate more ideas than groups without cues.

sources.locator: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 302), Sec. 5, opening paragraph
sources.quote: Dyads generated an average of 19.4 ideas across all groups.

estimates.notes: The paper reports the full-sample Cue-versus-NoCue result only in words. Its REML specification has Access-to-Cue, Modality and their interaction as fixed effects, with Prior Design Experience and Recycling Knowledge as random effects, and reports no significant factors. There are no printed arm means, SDs, coefficient, F statistic, p value, SE or CI. The overall mean in the source quotation pools all groups and cannot be entered as either arm mean. The record is retained with null statistics; absence of significance is not coded as a zero effect.

estimates.outcome: Homogenization across dyads (cosine distance of each idea from an average idea embedding)
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Each idea embedding is compared with an average idea embedding, using cosine distance as plotted in Fig. 6. The embedding model is not named. Sec. 6.3 describes a centroid within each condition, while App. A.4.1 describes an average over ideas across groups and distances to both Cue and NoCue ideas. The figure compares Cue Ideas and No Cue Ideas, pooling meeting modalities.

Homogenization analysis of ideas generated by groups with cues versus without cues.

estimates.notes: Figure only: the violin plot has no printed arm summary values or inferential result. No means, SDs, medians, quartiles, differences, p values, test statistics, SEs, CIs or analysis counts are transcribed from the plot. A Wilcoxon test is named, but its statistic and p value are not printed, so test is null and se_basis is not_reported. The named analysis operates on individual ideas, and no adjustment for their nesting within dyads is described. The main text calls the quantity cosine similarity; the figure and its caption identify cosine distance, so higher_is is more_diverse. Whether the centroid is condition-specific or pooled remains unresolved. The cue-homogeneity means and SDs later in Sec. 6.3 and Fig. 10 describe AI-generated cues, not these human-generated ideas.

open_items: People and dyads randomized per arm, people and dyads analyzed per outcome, and analyzed arm sizes are not printed. No count is inferred from degrees of freedom, balanced allocation, or exclusions.

PDF p. 5 (printed p. 300), Sec. 4.1.1 drops two discussions for echoes and two other sessions for technical issues, and excludes thirteen participants from analyses requiring missing background responses. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 302), footnote 12 describes seventy audio sessions, four echo exclusions and sixteen researcher-only recordings, without settling how those sets overlap.

The generation of the dyad-level idea-topic score is underspecified: methods describe each idea's entropy, whereas the reported comparison is between groups. Sec. 5.1.1 also calls its dependent variable the diversity of cues.

The printed SDs accompanying the two numerical topic contrasts concern dyad scores. The extraction template does not offer team as an sd_level code; those fields are null and the level is documented in notes.
The idea-count contrast has no numerical arm summaries or test result. Only the all-groups mean is printed.

The idea-homogenization outcome has no printed arm levels or Wilcoxon result. The embedding model, analysis count and whether the centroid pools both arms are unresolved; the text and appendix describe the centroid differently.
The paper does not state the model release year or explicitly identify the country where the participants were studied.
Random assignment is stated, but the exact allocation procedure and its relationship to demographic balancing are not described.
App. A.3.1 supplies a familiarity-building cue prompt, but the main text does not establish whether cued dyads also received AI assistance in that preceding task.
notes: Independent extractor B. The PDF figures and appendix were inspected, and the complete markdown conversion was read in chunks, including references and all appendix sections. Numerical outcome values were checked against PDF text with pymupdf and against in-memory rendered crops where the PDF text layer corrupted mathematical symbols. Source quotations use the visible printed mathematical notation, with line breaks joined. Only full-sample randomized assistance contrasts enter estimates. The paper's within-dyad topic diversity is coded flexibility; across-dyad semantic homogenization is a separate diversity outcome. The published study has no delayed unassisted outcome. Form sample_overlap identifies no shared participant sample. The OSF link in App. A.1 points to project data; no raw-data calculations were made. No means, differences, standard errors, effect sizes, or participant counts were computed. Supplementary post hoc p values and the all-groups idea-count mean are preserved in source quotations without duplicating contrasts.
